title: Rajahnate of Cebu
capsule: The Rajahnate of Cebu was a pre-colonial Visayan polity in the central Philippines, founded by Sri Lumay (Rajamuda Lumaya), a Sumatran prince of mixed Malay-Tamil descent who established his seat at Singhapala (modern Mabolo, Cebu City). Under Rajah Humabon the polity reached its greatest prominence as a regional trade hub receiving tribute from Siamese and other Southeast Asian partners; it was Humabon who witnessed Ferdinand Magellan's landing in 1521 and the Battle of Mactan in which Lapu-Lapu killed Magellan. Spanish conquistador Miguel López de Legazpi defeated Rajah Tupas in 1565, dissolving the rajahnate and establishing the first permanent Spanish settlement in the Philippines.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The rajahnate's core on Cebu island is secure; the extent of its tributary network across the Visayas is reconstructed from Spanish-era accounts and is approximate.
